title: Munchog (Great Pond Island)
summary: A Montauk island name in Great Pond, now Lake Montauk, connected with older forms such as Munchoage and Manchoage.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Lake Montauk island marker; needs map review
introduction_content: Munchog names an island in Great Pond at Montauk, now Lake Montauk. The placename study identifies it as the larger of the two islands in the pond.
history_content: Island placename, the Great Pond/Lake Montauk setting, and the island-name interpretation are brought together here. Time-specific town-account context is handled as a Historic Moment.
translation_content:
Alternate forms include Munchog, Munchoage, and Manchoage. The related Montauk form munchoage is interpreted as an island.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names represent the intangible heritage of a place – the stories of that place and the people who are part of that place.”

— First Peoples’ Cultural Council, Report on the First Peoples’ Cultural Council Indigenous Cultural Heritage Forum (2020), Theme 3: Indigenous Place-Naming, PDF page 27
whereintheworld_content: The point is an approximate marker for the larger island area in modern Lake Montauk, historically Great Pond. It is not a surveyed historical coordinate and should be reviewed against detailed historic and modern maps.
